name: Mintokling Guest House
summary: A long-running, family-feel guest house on Bhanu Path, just below the Secretariat road and about 10 minutes on foot from MG Marg. Quiet garden, simple rooms, and a good base for travellers who want central Gangtok without the noise of the market lanes.
body: Mintokling sits on Bhanu Path off Secretariat Road, a short uphill walk from MG Marg and Paljor Stadium. That location is the main reason we book it: you can walk to dinner, to the ropeway station at Tashiling and to the Sunday haat at Lal Bazaar without needing a taxi for every hop. The building is set back in a small garden, so nights are quieter than on the hotel strips near the taxi stands.

Rooms are plain and clean rather than fancy, with a choice of standard, superior and suite categories. Expect hot water, Wi-Fi and a simple breakfast. Parking is on site, which matters in Gangtok, where most central hotels have none. It suits budget couples, solo travellers and small families who will be out sightseeing all day and only need a reliable bed.
why: Walkable to MG Marg, the ropeway and Lal Bazaar
Garden setting, quieter than the market-side hotels
On-site parking, rare in central Gangtok

faqs.q: How far is Mintokling Guest House from MG Marg?
faqs.a: It is roughly 600–800 metres from MG Marg along Bhanu Path and Secretariat Road, about a 10-minute walk, with a short climb on the way back. Taxis wait at the nearby junction if you are carrying shopping or walking late. The ropeway's top station at Tashiling, beside the Secretariat, is also within walking distance.

faqs.q: Is Mintokling suitable for families with children?
faqs.a: Yes, for families who want a simple, quiet base. Rooms take two adults and one child, and the garden gives children some space. It has no pool, play area or lift, so families with very young children or older relatives who struggle with steps should ask us about room location before booking.

faqs.q: Can we book Tsomgo and Nathu La trips from Mintokling?
faqs.a: Yes. Like most Gangtok hotels, the front desk can connect you with registered taxi operators who arrange the Tsomgo and Baba Mandir permit a day ahead. If you book through us, we arrange the permit, car and driver and pick you up from the guest house gate. Check current status before you travel.

name: Hotel Sonam Delek
summary: A small Tibet Road hotel that has been running since the early 1990s, a 10-minute walk from MG Marg. Rooms have balconies facing the valley, and its restaurant is known locally for a Sikkimese thali. Good value for travellers who want a view without paying view-hotel prices.
body: Tibet Road was the old start of the trade route north and east towards the passes, and it is still one of the best streets in Gangtok to stay on: high enough for views, close enough to walk to MG Marg in about 10 minutes. Hotel Sonam Delek has worked here since the early 1990s, which makes it one of the older family hotels on the road.

Rooms are compact with wooden floors, French windows and small private balconies; on a clear morning between October and March you can see the Kangchenjunga range from the upper floors. Breakfast is included. The restaurant is the reason many people stay: ask for the Sikkimese thali with gundruk soup and local greens. Expect steps, no lift in some wings and simple bathrooms.
why: Valley-facing balconies at a budget price
Sikkimese thali in the in-house restaurant
Tibet Road location, walkable to MG Marg

faqs.q: Can you see Kangchenjunga from Hotel Sonam Delek?
faqs.a: On clear days, yes, from the valley-facing rooms on the upper floors. Views are most reliable from October to early March, usually in the first two hours after sunrise. From June to September, monsoon cloud hides the range on most days, so do not pay extra for a view room in those months.

faqs.q: Is Hotel Sonam Delek close to the taxi stand?
faqs.a: It is about 10–15 minutes on foot from MG Marg and the private taxi stands around Paljor Stadium Road, mostly level or downhill on the way there. Shared jeeps for North Sikkim and for Siliguri leave from separate stands outside the centre, so you will need a short local taxi ride to reach them.

faqs.q: Does Hotel Sonam Delek serve Sikkimese food?
faqs.a: Yes. The restaurant is known for its Sikkimese thali, which usually includes rice, dal, seasonal greens, gundruk (fermented leafy greens) soup and pickles. Order it a few hours ahead if you can, as some dishes are made in small batches. It is an easy, honest introduction to local food.

name: Martam village homestays
price_band: ≈ ₹1,500–2,500 per person a night with meals (indicative)
summary: Family homestays and small village guesthouses in Martam, a farming village of terraced paddy and cardamom about 29–34 km from Gangtok via Rumtek. Home-cooked meals, village walks and a night of real quiet, about an hour from the capital.
body: Martam is a Bhutia and Nepali farming village spread across a valley of terraced rice fields below Rumtek. Several families take guests in their homes or in small guesthouses next to them, and there are also a couple of resort-style properties in the valley. We list the village rather than one family because we match guests to the house that suits them: some have attached bathrooms and views, others are simpler and closer to village life.

A stay usually includes dinner and breakfast cooked in the family kitchen: rice, dal, local greens, perhaps a chicken or pork curry, homemade pickle and butter tea if you ask. Days are for walking between hamlets, visiting Rumtek and Sang monasteries and watching paddy planting (June–July) or harvest (October–November). Expect squat or western toilets depending on the house, and power cuts in storms.
why: One hour from Gangtok but a full change of pace
Meals cooked at home with produce from the farm
Easy walks to Rumtek, Sang and the terraced fields

faqs.q: How do we reach Martam homestays from Gangtok?
faqs.a: Martam is about 29–34 km from Gangtok, roughly 1–1.5 hours by car via Ranipool and Rumtek. A reserved small car costs about ₹1,500–2,000 one way. Shared jeeps run towards Rumtek and Sang from Gangtok, but times change, so most guests take a car. Your host can also arrange a pickup for a fee.

faqs.q: Are Martam homestays comfortable for older travellers?
faqs.a: Many are, if you choose the right house. Ask for a room with an attached western bathroom and few steps from the road, and avoid houses reached by long footpaths. Nights are mild at about 1,400 m, so cold is rarely a problem except in December and January, when hosts provide heavy quilts.

faqs.q: Do Martam homestays serve vegetarian food?
faqs.a: Yes. Most households cook vegetarian meals happily, as rice, dal, seasonal greens, potatoes, squash and soft churpi dishes are everyday food. Tell us in advance if you need no onion or garlic or are vegan, so the family can plan. Meat is usually chicken or pork, cooked only if you ask.

name: Netuk House
summary: A family-run heritage house on Tibet Road built in the late 1950s for Gellong Netuk Lama, a counsellor to the Chogyal. Traditional Sikkimese rooms, home-style Sikkimese food and views towards Kangchenjunga, a short walk above MG Marg.
body: Netuk House was built in the late 1950s as the home of Gellong Netuk Lama, who served as an executive counsellor to the Chogyal of Sikkim. It stands on Tibet Road, once the main route out of Gangtok for traders and travellers heading towards Tibet, and the family has run it as a guest house for decades. The building keeps its painted woodwork, carved window frames and Tibetan-style furnishings.

There are traditional and more modern rooms; ask for one with a balcony on the Kangchenjunga side. The kitchen is the heart of the place, serving Sikkimese and Tibetan home cooking, and guests often eat together. Expect older plumbing and staircases rather than lifts. It suits travellers who want to stay somewhere with a story, and it sits about 10 minutes on foot from MG Marg.
why: A real 1950s Gangtok house with royal-court history
Home-style Sikkimese and Tibetan cooking
Tibet Road location with mountain-side rooms

faqs.q: Who was Netuk Lama?
faqs.a: Gellong Netuk Lama was an executive counsellor to the Chogyal (king) of Sikkim in the 1950s, and Netuk House was his family home. The house was built on Tibet Road, the old route towards the Tibetan passes. His family still runs it as a guest house, and staff are usually happy to talk about its history.

faqs.q: Is Netuk House good for a honeymoon?
faqs.a: For couples who prefer character to luxury, yes. Rooms are warm and traditional, meals are home cooked and the house is quiet in the evenings. It has no spa, pool or room service menu of a large resort. If those matter, look at Elgin Nor-Khill or the Taj and Mayfair resorts instead.

faqs.q: Is Netuk House within walking distance of MG Marg?
faqs.a: Yes. It is about 10 minutes on foot from MG Marg along Tibet Road, mostly downhill on the way into town and uphill on the way back. Cafés, Lal Bazaar and the Paljor Stadium Road taxi stands are all within 15–20 minutes' walk, so you will rarely need a car in town.

name: The Hidden Forest Retreat
summary: A family-run guest house in Middle Sichey, about 2 km from central Gangtok, set in roughly three acres of garden built around an orchid nursery the family started decades ago. Meals use produce from the farm. Good for garden lovers and birders who want calm near town.
body: The Hidden Forest Retreat is in Middle Sichey, on the north side of Gangtok, about 2 km from the centre. The family began an orchid nursery here around three decades ago, and the guest house grew up around it: about three acres of trees, bamboo, ferns, lilies and orchid houses. Birds and butterflies use the garden, and early mornings are worth getting up for.

Rooms are large doubles in a traditional style. Meals are cooked from fresh local produce, much of it grown in the garden, and the hosts can arrange a taste of chhaang (millet beer) for guests who are curious. Spring (March to May) is the best season for flowering orchids, but something is in bloom in most months. You will need a short taxi ride into town.
why: Orchid nursery and three-acre garden on site
Home cooking from the family's own produce
Quiet, 2 km from the centre of Gangtok

faqs.q: When is the best time to see orchids at Hidden Forest Retreat?
faqs.a: March to May is peak flowering for most of the orchids in the nursery and garden, with spring rhododendrons and magnolias around Gangtok at the same time. Some species flower in late summer and autumn too, so there is usually something in bloom. Ask the hosts for a walk through the nursery.

faqs.q: How far is Hidden Forest Retreat from MG Marg?
faqs.a: It is about 2 km from MG Marg in Middle Sichey, roughly 10 minutes by taxi depending on traffic. A local taxi ride costs about ₹150–250. Walking is possible but involves steep sections, so most guests use taxis to get into town in the evening and walk only in daylight.

faqs.q: Is Hidden Forest Retreat good for birdwatching?
faqs.a: It is one of the better places to stay in Gangtok for casual birding, because the garden and nearby forest attract common Himalayan species such as bulbuls, sunbirds and laughingthrushes. Serious birders combine it with a morning at Fambong Lho or Kyongnosla, which we can arrange with a local naturalist.

name: Hotel Tibet
image_query: Hotel Tibet Gangtok Paljor Stadium Road
summary: An established mid-range hotel on Paljor Stadium Road, a few minutes' walk from MG Marg, decorated in a traditional Tibetan style. Suites and deluxe rooms face the valley and, on clear days, Kangchenjunga. A dependable choice for families who want central Gangtok with a lift and a restaurant.
body: Hotel Tibet stands on Paljor Stadium Road, the busy road that runs below MG Marg, so you can be on the promenade in five minutes and at the taxi stands even sooner. It has been a Gangtok fixture for decades, with Tibetan carpets, painted pillars and thangka-style decoration throughout, and a traditional-style hall used for meetings and family events.

The valley-side suites and deluxe rooms are worth the small extra: on clear mornings from October to March they look across to the Kangchenjunga range. The restaurant covers Tibetan, Indian and Chinese dishes. Road-side rooms can hear traffic until late evening, so ask for the valley side. It suits families and older travellers who want a central, straightforward hotel.
why: Five minutes' walk from MG Marg
Traditional Tibetan interiors
Valley-facing rooms with mountain views

faqs.q: Is Hotel Tibet in the centre of Gangtok?
faqs.a: Yes. It is on Paljor Stadium Road, just below MG Marg, about a five-minute walk from the promenade. Restaurants, banks, the taxi stands and Lal Bazaar are all close. That makes it practical for families who do not want to depend on taxis for every short trip in town.

faqs.q: Which rooms at Hotel Tibet have mountain views?
faqs.a: The suites and deluxe rooms on the valley side have the views, including Kangchenjunga on clear days between October and March. Road-side rooms are cheaper and can be noisier in the evening. When we book, we request valley-side rooms, but final allocation is the hotel's decision on arrival.

faqs.q: Is Hotel Tibet a good base for Tsomgo Lake and Nathu La?
faqs.a: Yes. Tsomgo cars leave from central Gangtok early in the morning, and Paljor Stadium Road is an easy pickup point. Permits are arranged a day ahead through registered agents with your ID and photos. Nathu La is for Indian nationals only and usually closed on Mondays and Tuesdays. Check current status before you travel.

name: The Chumbi Residency
summary: One of Gangtok's best-known mid-range hotels, open since 1997 on Tibet Road, five minutes' walk above MG Marg. Consistent service, valley and Kangchenjunga views from the upper floors, and the Tangerine restaurant and bar. A safe choice for couples and families stepping up from budget hotels.
body: The Chumbi Residency opened in 1997 and has kept a steady reputation for nearly three decades, which in Gangtok's fast-changing hotel scene says a lot. It sits on Tibet Road above the market, about five minutes' walk from MG Marg, and its name looks across the border to the Chumbi Valley, where the Chogyals once kept a summer palace.

Rooms come in two main categories, with the better ones facing the valley and, on clear mornings, the Kangchenjunga range. The Tangerine restaurant and bar serves Indian, continental and Sikkimese dishes, and there are meeting rooms for small events. Service is the strong point: staff are used to arranging permits, early breakfasts for Tsomgo days and late check-outs. It is a comfortable, central base.
why: Running since 1997 with consistent service
Five minutes' walk from MG Marg
Upper-floor rooms with Kangchenjunga views

faqs.q: Where is The Chumbi Residency in Gangtok?
faqs.a: It is on Tibet Road, above the main market, about a five-minute walk from MG Marg. The walk into town is downhill; the return is a short climb. Taxis can reach the door, which helps on arrival with luggage and on early Tsomgo or North Sikkim departures.

faqs.q: Why is it called Chumbi?
faqs.a: The Chumbi Valley is the Tibetan valley just across Nathu La and Cho La from Sikkim. The Chogyals of Sikkim kept a summer palace there, and the old trade routes from Gangtok led through it. The hotel takes its name from that valley.

faqs.q: Is The Chumbi Residency good for families?
faqs.a: Yes. It is central, has a restaurant on site, and staff are used to families and older travellers, arranging early breakfasts and packed meals for long excursion days. Ask for a valley-facing room and tell us about any mobility needs so we can request a room with fewer steps.

name: The Elgin Nor-Khill
summary: Built in 1932 as the royal guest house of the Chogyal of Sikkim, Nor-Khill sits in its own gardens beside Paljor Stadium in central Gangtok. Heads of state stayed here; today Elgin Hotels runs it as a heritage hotel with Sikkimese decor and old-world service.
body: Nor-Khill was built in 1932 for the Chogyal of Sikkim as the kingdom's royal guest house, and visiting heads of state and dignitaries stayed here before 1975. The name is usually translated as 'house of precious things'. The Chogyal is said to have liked painting in its garden, which is still the heart of the property. The Oberoi family (B.R. Oberoi) acquired it in 1975, and Elgin Hotels runs it today.

Rooms mix Sikkimese and Tibetan details with colonial-era proportions, and the public rooms hold old photographs and royal-era objects. It sits beside Paljor Stadium, a 10-minute walk from MG Marg, yet the garden feels removed from the traffic. It suits couples and older travellers who value history and service over modern resort facilities.
why: Royal guest house of the Chogyals, built in 1932
Gardens in the middle of town
Old-world service and Sikkimese decor

faqs.q: What is the history of Elgin Nor-Khill?
faqs.a: Nor-Khill was built in 1932 as the royal guest house of the Chogyal of Sikkim and hosted visiting heads of state and dignitaries. In 1975, the year Sikkim became an Indian state, it was acquired by B.R. Oberoi of the Oberoi hotel family. It is now run by Elgin Hotels as a heritage hotel.

faqs.q: How far is Elgin Nor-Khill from MG Marg?
faqs.a: It is about a 10-minute walk from MG Marg, beside Paljor Stadium. The walk is mostly gentle, with a short climb on the way back. Taxis are easy to find on Paljor Stadium Road, and the hotel can arrange cars for sightseeing, Tsomgo and Nathu La.

faqs.q: Is Elgin Nor-Khill good for a honeymoon?
faqs.a: It works well for couples who like history, gardens and quiet evenings in the middle of town. It is a heritage hotel rather than a large resort, so do not expect a big pool or extensive spa. For resort-style facilities, look at Mayfair at Lower Samdur or Taj Guras Kutir at Pangthang.

name: Mayfair Spa Resort & Casino Gangtok
summary: A five-star resort at Lower Samdur near Ranipool, about 10 km below central Gangtok on the NH10 side, with a full spa, a casino and landscaped grounds. The choice for travellers who want a resort stay with everything on site rather than a hotel in the town.
body: Mayfair sits at Lower Samdur, near Ranipool, roughly 20–30 minutes' drive below central Gangtok depending on traffic. Being out of town is the point: the resort is spread across landscaped grounds with Sikkimese-style buildings, a large spa and a licensed casino, and you can spend a full day here without leaving. It is also slightly lower and warmer than Gangtok, which helps in winter.

Rooms and suites are large, service is polished and the restaurants cover Indian, Asian and continental food. The trade-off is distance: every trip into Gangtok means a car, and evening strolls on MG Marg take planning. We suggest it for the last two nights of a trip, after the high passes, when a spa and a slow morning are welcome.
why: Full spa and on-site casino
Landscaped resort grounds outside the town
Easy access to the Siliguri road for departure

faqs.q: How far is Mayfair Gangtok from MG Marg?
faqs.a: Mayfair is at Lower Samdur near Ranipool, about 10 km from MG Marg. The drive usually takes 20–30 minutes, longer at evening rush hour. A taxi into town costs about ₹500–700 each way. The resort can arrange cars, and we include transfers when we book it as part of a package.

faqs.q: Does Mayfair Gangtok have a casino?
faqs.a: Yes, the resort has a licensed casino, and it is one of the few places in Sikkim with one. Entry rules, minimum ages and dress codes are set by the casino and can change, so check current status before you travel. Many guests come for the spa and gardens and never visit the casino.

faqs.q: Is Mayfair a good choice for a honeymoon in Sikkim?
faqs.a: Yes, for couples who want resort facilities: spa treatments, large rooms and grounds to walk in. It suits the end of a trip after North Sikkim or Tsomgo. If you prefer to walk to cafés and MG Marg in the evening, combine one or two nights here with a central Gangtok hotel.

name: Taj Guras Kutir Resort & Spa, Gangtok
summary: IHCL's Taj resort in the Pangthang forest, about 20 minutes' drive from Gangtok, opened in September 2023. 69 rooms and villas across 14 acres, Sikkimese-inspired architecture, a spa and views to Kangchenjunga. Gangtok's newest top-end address, named after the guras, Sikkim's rhododendron.
body: Taj Guras Kutir opened on 25 September 2023 in the forest at Pangthang, above Gangtok on the road north, roughly 20 minutes' drive from the centre. Indian Hotels Company (IHCL) built 69 keys across about 14 acres, with architecture that borrows from Sikkimese buildings: sloping roofs, carved and painted wood and local stone. Guras is the Nepali word for rhododendron, Sikkim's state tree, which flowers across these hills in spring.

Rooms face the forest or the Kangchenjunga range, and the resort has a spa and several dining options. Pangthang is cooler and quieter than town, and close to Tashi View Point and Hanuman Tok. As with any resort outside Gangtok, plan a car for evenings on MG Marg. It is the top choice for couples and families who want premium comfort.
why: Opened 2023: Gangtok's newest luxury resort
14 acres of forest at Pangthang with Kangchenjunga views
Sikkimese-inspired architecture and a full spa

faqs.q: Where is Taj Guras Kutir in Gangtok?
faqs.a: It is in the Pangthang forest area, above Gangtok on the road towards North Sikkim, about 20 minutes' drive from the town centre. Tashi View Point and Hanuman Tok are close by. A taxi into MG Marg costs about ₹600–900 each way, and the resort can arrange cars.

faqs.q: When did Taj Guras Kutir open?
faqs.a: IHCL opened Taj Guras Kutir Resort & Spa on 25 September 2023. It has 69 rooms, suites and villas across roughly 14 acres. Because it is new, rooms and facilities are in very good condition, and rates are among the highest in Gangtok, especially in October and from April to early June.

faqs.q: Is Taj Guras Kutir worth it compared with hotels in town?
faqs.a: It is worth it if the stay itself is part of the holiday: forest setting, views, spa and Taj service. If you plan to spend evenings on MG Marg and want to walk everywhere, a central hotel such as Elgin Nor-Khill or Chumbi Residency is more practical and costs much less.
